task-build-pre.md: Read this project's AGENTS.md, README, package scripts, workspace/build documentation and existing release scripts. Discover the correct build and meaningful validation commands yourself; do not ask the user to author a Flow or provide commands already in the project. Build an acceptance artifact containing the retained delivery. Preserve source files and the original commit policy. Do not switch services, merge, commit or push during build. If prerequisites are genuinely missing, publish a structured blocked result describing the exact missing capability. Record actual commands, checks, artifact path and version; never invent success.
task-build-post.md: Verify the candidate artifact and version from actual project output. Report its location, checks and limitations through session_report with type result and a structured payload. Do not mark manual acceptance complete.
task-deploy-pre.md: If an explicit project deployment declaration selects the host service controller, the platform performs version replacement from the frozen approval without a Session command. Do not duplicate it. Otherwise Read the project's existing deployment/service management scripts and the approved candidate version in the frozen context section. This is a separately confirmed maintenance action. Replace only the declared current service, stopping the old instance before starting the candidate on the same address; never run two instances against the same data. Preserve a rollback path and verify the actual health version. Do not bypass sandbox or deployment permissions. If the required host service-control capability is unavailable, return status blocked with the exact reason; do not guess PIDs, kill unrelated processes, start a second service, or claim a successful switch.
task-deploy-post.md: Verify the current service is healthy and matches the approved candidate. Record the actual version and verification evidence. If the switch failed, follow the project's authorized rollback procedure and report failure. A chat statement is not deployment evidence.
task-integrate-pre.md: Read the approved merge plan, original decision/task context, source/target versions and user choices from the frozen context section. This is a separately confirmed target integration action; original delivery restrictions remain in force. Preserve the source worktree and its commit policy. Integrate only the approved changes into the declared target, using existing project procedures. Do not alter user choices, discard target changes, force-push, delete worktrees or modify unrelated branches. Any additional conflict, changed input or missing capability requires a blocked result and a fresh user decision. Preserve task attribution trailers where available.
task-integrate-post.md: Run the relevant project validation and inspect the actual target HEAD and Git state. Publish the approved operation ID, original source/target versions, resulting targetHead, summary and evidence. Do not clean the worktree or change the original task's acceptance conclusion. Report blocked/failed instead of claiming success when verification is incomplete.
operation.md:
# Admitted maintenance operation

Read context.operation for phase, operationId, sourceVersion, targetVersion, approval, resources and receiptPath. Continue the same Session and retained worktree. Discover commands from project files and existing scripts. Only the declared operation is admitted; preserve the frozen commit and target policy.

For build/deploy generate or reuse an operation-scoped, idempotent script and a frozen manifest under the receipt directory. Persist operation ID, exact input versions, candidate version, approval and recovery procedure before side effects. For build, bounded foreground execution through the existing authorized project capability is sufficient. For deploy, use an existing authorized project controller or executor that survives the old httpd exiting; if the host has selected its persistent service controller, it performs the switch directly and no Session command is required. Do not depend on a browser connection, old httpd process, bare background shell, guessed PID or MCP credentials embedded in a script. If this execution capability is unavailable, publish blocked with the exact missing capability. Never add a new privileged service-control API or escalate permissions yourself.

For replacement stop the declared old service and start only the approved candidate. The independent executor must continue health checks after the old httpd exits, verify actual running version and preserve rollback evidence. Persist progress and the terminal receipt; MCP notifications only accelerate observation. If Cells or its runner also exits, reconcile the saved operation and actual service before any retry. Do not replay a script with an unknown outcome.

For build/deploy atomically rename a temporary file to context.operation.receiptPath. The immutable receipt and session_report result must contain the identical payload:
{schema:"nestos.kanban.operation-result/1",operationId:<exact ID>,sourceVersion:<frozen sourceVersion>,targetVersion:<frozen targetVersion>,status:"succeeded"|"blocked"|"failed",version:<actual candidate/running version>,evidence:{path:<project-relative build manifest or receipt outside _nestos/kanban>,sha256:<actual file hash>},summary:<actual checks and limitations>}
Build success requires real artifact evidence. Deploy success requires healthy actual running version matching the approved candidate. Script exit, chat text, a receipt or MCP acknowledgment alone is insufficient. Never invent success.

For integration use the same result schema and frozen versions, with targetHead set to the verified resulting HEAD; only approved conflict choices are allowed. For missing context use session_request and yield without a final result. Publish the terminal payload once through session_report({id:<stable-id>,message:{type:"result",content:<short summary>,payload:<same result>}}); preserve its ID and content on retries.
